newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends down sharply on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends down sharply on speculation.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended down sharply on Tuesday on institutional speculation with few retail investors daring to buy given the thin volume, traders said.
The key October contract ended at an intra-day low of 1,885 yuan ($227) per tonne, losing 200 yuan. It opened at 2,000 yuan and hit a high of 2,010.
December fell nine yuan to 2,010 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 1,200 tonnes from 1,100.
Traders said institutions pushed prices sharply down with few retail investors daring to enter the market.
"Retail investors who buy will suffer heavy losses with the market so dominated by institutions," one trader said. "As a result the hot money has flowed over into more active markets."
Traders said futures prices were completely under the control of institutions despite higher spot prices.
The price of spot rice is now around 2,400 yuan per tonne.
"It is hard to forecast the trend for rice but it will stay below the spot price for the time being," a second trader said.
